subject: TridentWorks: Zero-Trust VPC peering & on-prem package — implementation plan
messages:

Cc: Priya Singh <priya@tridentworks.io>
Date: 2028-07-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TridentWorks: Zero-Trust VPC peering & on-prem package — implementation plan

Kimberly — thanks for the quick follow. A couple high-level constraints from our side before we lock dates:
- We have strict zero-trust rules; all outbound egress must go through our proxy layer (10.240.0.0/22).
- Our primary VPC CIDR is 10.1.0.0/16; we'll need to confirm whether Redwood prefers the peering to be from a dedicated services VPC or direct into our app VPC.
- Maintenance window: prefer weekends (Sat 02:00–06:00 PDT) for any host-level changes.

I've looped in netops for CIDR confirmation and firewall documentation. Can you send the on-prem installer manifest and the high-level network diagram you mentioned?

— Alex
TridentWorks, Sr. Cloud Architect
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@tridentworks.io>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Subject: TridentWorks: Zero-Trust VPC peering & on-prem package — implementation plan

Alex — thanks for the constraints, and welcome Priya + netops. High level response below and attached are the items you asked for.

Attachments: trident_network_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram), onprem_install_manifest.xlsx (installer variables), redwood_vpc_peering_template.json (Peering template + ACL examples)

Quick notes:
- We recommend peering into a dedicated Redwood services VPC (we can route only the model-serving subnets). This keeps control plane separation and minimizes blast radius.
- For zero-trust egress, Redwood components support egress via customer-managed proxies; in our installer you can provide HTTP proxy settings and certs.
- For the weekend maintenance window you proposed, Marcus is available for the first two Saturdays of August (Aug 5, Aug 12, 02:00–06:00 PDT). Please confirm which you prefer.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kickoff call with Network Ops and Site Reliability (30 min) — proposed Thu Jul 26, 10:00 PDT.
2) Exchange finalized CIDRs and firewall rule set (via shared Drive doc).
3) Dry-run install in staging during weekday window; production cutover on agreed weekend.

I will hand this off to Grace (CS lead) and Marcus (implementation eng) to drive the runbook and network checklist.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — received the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions before the kickoff: 
1) Does the onprem_install_manifest.xlsx include keys for our HSM/KMS integration, or is that a separate step?
2) For private endpoints, do you create AWS Interface Endpoints in the customer's account or provide a CNAMED private DNS for Redwood-managed endpoints?
3) Is there a short list of ports/protocols that must be opened from our proxy layer to the Redwood services VPC?

We'll confirm CIDRs by EOD tomorrow. Also, Priya from our procurement team will open a SOW ticket if we proceed — do you have a template or should we start from the HubSpot deal record?

— Priya
Director of IT Ops, TridentWorks
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@tridentworks.io>, Alex Torres <alex.torres@tridentworks.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TridentWorks: Zero-Trust VPC peering & on-prem package — implementation plan

Hi Priya / Alex — Grace stepping in to handle the onboarding cadence and SOW coordination. Quick answers: 
- HSM/KMS: we support customer-managed keys. The onprem_install_manifest includes placeholders for KMS key IDs; the actual key provisioning is a separate step with our Security team. We will not have access to your private keys.
- Private endpoints: Redwood supports both models. For AWS we can either create Interface Endpoints in your account (preferred for low-latency internal traffic) or configure Redwood-managed private DNS if you prefer our VPC to host endpoints. We recommend creating the Interface Endpoints in your account for tighter control.
- Ports/protocols: minimal list below — this is what to allow from your proxy layer to Redwood services VPC:
  * TCP 443 (TLS) outbound to the model serving frontends
  * TCP 1024-1030 (optional) for internal health probes (can be locked down by source IP)
  * UDP 53 to internal resolver if using private DNS (optional)

SOW: please start from the HubSpot deal (HS-42319); I'll share a skeleton SOW and a procurement checklist in the drive folder.

I'll schedule the Thu Jul 26 kickoff at 10:00 PDT and send calendar invites to netops and our implementation leads. Marcus will own the staging dry-run and Soojin will own the network acceptance tests.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: TridentWorks Network Ops <netops@tridentworks.io>, Priya Singh <priya@tridentworks.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-26T10:31:00-07:00
Subject: Network checklist & acceptance tests — TridentWorks private deploy

Hi all — following the kickoff, attaching a compact checklist we'll use during staging and production. High level items below; full checklist is in the Drive folder.

Network checklist (staging -> prod):
- CIDR confirmation: TridentWorks app VPC 10.1.0.0/16; services VPC proposed 10.2.0.0/16 (customer-owned).
- Peering model: customer creates peering connection; Redwood requests route table updates for model-serving subnets only.
- IP ranges allowed from proxy: 10.240.0.0/22 (confirmed).
- Interface endpoints: customer to provision com.redwood.service and com.redwood.control (interface endpoints in customer account).
- Firewall rules: outbound 443 to service FQDNs; health probe TCP 1025 from our IPs (see redwood_vpc_peering_template.json).
- MTU and path-MTU tests recommended before cutover.
- KMS/HSM: bring-your-own-keys workflow documented; key IDs must be provided in installer manifest.

Acceptance tests (examples):
1) TLS handshake and certificate validation to model frontends from inside customer VPC.
2) Tokenized inference call: sample prompt, ensure latencies < 300ms for 512-token seq in staging.
3) KV cache warm-up and eviction behavior with 1M-prefetch workload.

Proposed schedule: staging dry-run Wed Aug 2, 02:00–04:00 PDT; production cutover Sat Aug 5, 02:00–06:00 PDT. Please confirm availability for those windows or propose Aug 12 if not possible.

Attachments referenced: redwood_vpc_peering_template.json, onprem_install_manifest.xlsx

— Soojin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
